newsitem.title: UK: N.Ireland Electricity down on MMC request.
newsitem.headline: N.Ireland Electricity down on MMC request.

text.p: Shares in Northern Ireland Electricity Plc fell on Friday after the company requested that the regulator's price review be reffered to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission.
The shares were down 15-1/2p at 327-1/2p by 0745 GMT.
"Most people felt that they would swallow the proposals from the regulator and hopefully give shareholders some benefit through share buybacks," said Nigel Hawkins analyst at Yamaichi.
"There's less chance of a buyback now," he said "You can't go to the MMC one minute then push the boat out in terms of shareholder benefits the next."
The regional electricity company said it had requested the MMC review after regulator Douglas Mclldoon rejected compromise proposals from the company.

Mclldoon wanted Northern Ireland Electricity to cut its distribution and transmission charges, its main source of revenue, by a one-off 30 percent next year. Future price rises were to be capped by two percent below inflation.
"They decided the pill is too bitter to swallow and to take their chance with the MMC," Hawkins said. "But the MMC may widen its enquiry to include the generation side as well."
